references.text: Moses' law commands that a worker should receive their wages on the same day – the principle that the worker is worthy of their wages, which Jesus here applies to preachers of the gospel.
The command not to withhold a worker's wages overnight reflects the same principle Jesus states: the worker is worthy of their wages.
In Matthew's mission discourse, Jesus gives similar instructions to the disciples to stay in the house they enter and that the worker is worthy of their food.
Paul argues that those who preach the gospel have a right to live from the gospel, using the principle that the worker deserves their wages.
Paul directly quotes this saying of Jesus: "The worker is worthy of their wages", as a Scripture alongside Deut 25:4.
At the first sending out of the twelve, Jesus gave similar instructions: "Stay in the house you enter and do not go elsewhere" – parallel to the instruction here.
Paul's advice to eat what is set before you reflects Jesus' instruction to the disciples to eat and drink what the hosts offer.
"You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out grain" – a principle that supports Jesus' statement that the worker is worthy of their wages, used by Paul in 1 Tim 5:18 and 1 Cor 9:9.
